items.prompt:
The reason a document was written is its:
A) purpose
B) font
C) page count

A persuasive technique like vivid imagery or repetition is a:
A) rhetorical feature
B) spelling rule
C) margin

A recurring idea such as liberty in a document is a:
A) theme
B) typo
C) page number

The Declaration grounds its case in 'self-evident' truths about equality. This expresses the theme of:
A) human equality and natural rights
B) royal power
C) military rule
items.answer: A) human equality and natural rights

solution.answer: A) human equality and natural rights

items.prompt:
A nineteenth-century abolitionist speech uses vivid imagery of chains. Its PURPOSE is to:
A) rouse the audience against slavery
B) describe metalwork
C) set tax rates
items.answer: A) rouse the audience against slavery

steps: Move against slavery. Key is A.
solution.answer: A) rouse the audience against slavery

items.prompt:
Why analyze these documents for themes, purposes, AND rhetorical features?
A) to understand their ideas and their persuasive craft
B) only to count pages
C) to ignore their meaning
items.answer: A) to understand their ideas and their persuasive craft

solution.answer: A) to understand their ideas and their persuasive craft

items.prompt:
Calling foundational truths 'self-evident' functions rhetorically to:
A) present the premises as beyond dispute, strengthening the argument
B) admit the premises are weak
C) change the subject
items.answer: A) present the premises as beyond dispute, strengthening the argument

solution.answer: A) present the premises as beyond dispute, strengthening the argument

items.prompt:
An eighteenth-century founding document and a nineteenth-century abolitionist text both engage the theme of:
A) liberty and equality
B) unrelated topics
C) only taxation

steps: Shared founding themes. Key is A.
